You are helping me finish ONE increment of a student project called IMS-HE (Information Management System for Hardware Enterprise). Stack: Laravel 13 (PHP ^8.3), Blade views, SQLite in development (MySQL in production), plain inline CSS inside resources/views/layouts/app.blade.php (there is NO Vite build, do not add npm or Vite), PHPUnit feature tests.

Conventions you must follow: thin controllers, business logic in app/Services, DB::transaction for changes to several tables, role checks with the RoleMiddleware (role:Treasurer,President) in routes/web.php, models in app/Models with primary keys named like product_id (always give the key names in relationships), staff use the web guard and customers use a guard called customer. Roles: Administrator (accounts only, never business modules), President, Treasurer, Inventory Clerk, Store Supervisor, Employee, Pending.

REUSE what already exists, do not recreate it: App\Support\Money and the global money() helper for pesos (always show money as ₱1,234.50 and parse typed money with Money::parse); Blade components x-alert (flash and validation messages), x-field, x-select and x-required-note (every new form starts with x-required-note and uses x-field and x-select, so inputs are aligned and required fields are marked); App\Support\CsvExporter; App\Models\AuditLog::record(action, table, recordId, userId) for the audit trail; InventoryService::deduct and add (int productId, int qty, string referenceType, int referenceId); the transaction and ValidationException style of CheckoutService and OrderManagementService; the PDF approach already used by ReportController::downloadSales and its PDF view.

HARD RULES:
1. DATABASE IS FROZEN: no new migration, no edit to any migration, no new table or column, no change to seeded data. Use only the tables and columns that exist. If you think a schema change is needed, STOP and ask me.
2. PURE INCREMENT: add new files and add only the minimum lines to existing shared files (routes/web.php, layouts/app.blade.php sidebar, routes/console.php, and the one service or controller line named in the task). Do not refactor, rename, reformat or "improve" working code. Do not change the Export Center, the UI kit, the catalog, the cart, checkout, products, categories, suppliers, purchase orders, deliveries or the auth screens unless the task names the exact line.
3. No new composer or npm packages.
4. Never touch .env, vendor, storage or database/database.sqlite. You may run php artisan migrate:fresh --seed on the local SQLite database.
5. Every task ends with: PHPUnit feature tests for each behavior (including a failure and a role-403 case), the result of php artisan test, and a list of every file you created or changed with one line each. Fix only failures that your task caused; list the other failures for me.
6. If anything is unclear or contradicts the code, ask me before guessing.
7. When the task is finished, STOP and wait. Do not start the next task.
